_comment: Single source of truth for the toolchain that produces a release (§51).
The reproducible-builds doc (https://docs.xchain.io/components/wallet/reproducible-builds)
makes the central claim that 'the toolchain version is part
of the output': a verifier who builds with a different Node than the release
lane used gets different bytes and cannot tell that apart from tampering. That
claim only holds if one version is pinned for BOTH, which is what this file is.
It was not pinned before. The release lanes asked actions/setup-node for major
'22', which resolves to whatever 22.x is newest ON THE DAY THE LANE RUNS, while
packages/desktop/Dockerfile pinned an exact (and different, and by then EOL for
our engines field) 20.18.0. Two releases cut a month apart used different Node
patches, a verifier got a third, and every resulting diff read as supply-chain
tampering to anyone following the published protocol.
Consumers, all of which test/smoke/audits/reproducible-toolchain.smoke.js holds
to this file:
- packages/desktop/Dockerfile      ARG NODE_VERSION / ARG NODE_SHA256_X64
- .github/workflows/release.yml    every actions/setup-node node-version
- packages/desktop/scripts/*.sh    asserted at runtime inside the container
Bumping Node is therefore a deliberate edit here plus a re-run of the
reproduction, and it invalidates pre-signing hashes published against the old
pin exactly the way an electron-builder major does.

node._versionNote: 22.x because the repo's engines field requires >=22 and the suites silently skip off it. Exact patch because a floating major is not a pin.
node._sha256Note: Only linux-x64 is listed because the reproduce container is amd64-only (see baseImage). Verified against https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.23.2/SHASUMS256.txt.

_platformNote: This digest's index carries exactly one real manifest, linux/amd64, so the
container is amd64 and nothing else. That is deliberate rather than a
limitation to fix: the release lane runs on ubuntu-latest (amd64) and
cross-builds the arm64 artifact from there, so an arm64 container would
reproduce a build we never cut. reproduce.sh passes --platform explicitly
so an arm64 verifier emulates on purpose instead of by accident.

_linuxArchesNote: Both are SHIPPED (spec §2) so both must be reproduced. build.sh and the release lane's linux job must build this same set; before this pin build.sh took no arch flags and covered x64 only, leaving the arm64 bundle with no published pre-signing hash at all.

sourceDateEpoch._note: Author date, matching the release lane. reproduce.sh used %ct (committer date); those differ on any rebased or amended commit, which is 10 of the last 200 commits here, up to 36 minutes apart. A verifier hitting one of those tags got different asar mtimes and a diff that looked exactly like tampering.
